120 def getfuncargnames(
121     function: Callable[..., Any],
122     *,
123     name: str = "",
124     is_method: bool = False,
125     cls: Optional[type] = None,
126 ) -> Tuple[str, ...]:
127     """Return the names of a function's mandatory arguments.
128 
129     Should return the names of all function arguments that:
130     * Aren't bound to an instance or type as in instance or class methods.
131     * Don't have default values.
132     * Aren't bound with functools.partial.
133     * Aren't replaced with mocks.
134 
135     The is_method and cls arguments indicate that the function should
136     be treated as a bound method even though it's not unless, only in
137     the case of cls, the function is a static method.
138 
139     The name parameter should be the original name in which the function was collected.
140     """
141     # TODO(RonnyPfannschmidt): This function should be refactored when we
142     # revisit fixtures. The fixture mechanism should ask the node for
143     # the fixture names, and not try to obtain directly from the
144     # function object well after collection has occurred.
145 
146     # The parameters attribute of a Signature object contains an
147     # ordered mapping of parameter names to Parameter instances.  This
148     # creates a tuple of the names of the parameters that don't have
149     # defaults.
150     try:
151         parameters = signature(function).parameters
152     except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
153         from _pytest.outcomes import fail
154 
155         fail(
156             f"Could not determine arguments of {function!r}: {e}",
157             pytrace=False,
158         )
159 
160     arg_names = tuple(
161         p.name
162         for p in parameters.values()
163         if (
164             p.kind is Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD
165             or p.kind is Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY
166         )
167         and p.default is Parameter.empty
168     )
169     if not name:
170         name = function.__name__
171 
172     # If this function should be treated as a bound method even though
173     # it's passed as an unbound method or function, remove the first
174     # parameter name.
175     if is_method or (
176         # Not using `getattr` because we don't want to resolve the staticmethod.
177         # Not using `cls.__dict__` because we want to check the entire MRO.
178         cls
179         and not isinstance(
180             inspect.getattr_static(cls, name, default=None), staticmethod
181         )
182     ):
183         arg_names = arg_names[1:]
184     # Remove any names that will be replaced with mocks.
185     if hasattr(function, "__wrapped__"):
186         arg_names = arg_names[num_mock_patch_args(function) :]
187     return arg_names
188

221 def ascii_escaped(val: Union[bytes, str]) -> str:
222     r"""If val is pure ASCII, return it as an str, otherwise, escape
223     bytes objects into a sequence of escaped bytes:
224 
225     b'\xc3\xb4\xc5\xd6' -> r'\xc3\xb4\xc5\xd6'
226 
227     and escapes unicode objects into a sequence of escaped unicode
228     ids, e.g.:
229 
230     r'4\nV\U00043efa\x0eMXWB\x1e\u3028\u15fd\xcd\U0007d944'
231 
232     Note:
233        The obvious "v.decode('unicode-escape')" will return
234        valid UTF-8 unicode if it finds them in bytes, but we
235        want to return escaped bytes for any byte, even if they match
236        a UTF-8 string.
237     """
238     if isinstance(val, bytes):
239         ret = _bytes_to_ascii(val)
240     else:
241         ret = val.encode("unicode_escape").decode("ascii")
242     return _translate_non_printable(ret)

246 class _PytestWrapper:
247     """Dummy wrapper around a function object for internal use only.
248 
249     Used to correctly unwrap the underlying function object when we are
250     creating fixtures, because we wrap the function object ourselves with a
251     decorator to issue warnings when the fixture function is called directly.
252     """
253 
254     obj = attr.ib()
255 
256 
257 def get_real_func(obj):
258     """Get the real function object of the (possibly) wrapped object by
259     functools.wraps or functools.partial."""
260     start_obj = obj
261     for i in range(100):
262         # __pytest_wrapped__ is set by @pytest.fixture when wrapping the fixture function
263         # to trigger a warning if it gets called directly instead of by pytest: we don't
264         # want to unwrap further than this otherwise we lose useful wrappings like @mock.patch (#3774)
265         new_obj = getattr(obj, "__pytest_wrapped__", None)
266         if isinstance(new_obj, _PytestWrapper):
267             obj = new_obj.obj
268             break
269         new_obj = getattr(obj, "__wrapped__", None)
270         if new_obj is None:
271             break
272         obj = new_obj
273     else:
274         from _pytest._io.saferepr import saferepr
275 
276         raise ValueError(
277             ("could not find real function of {start}\nstopped at {current}").format(
278                 start=saferepr(start_obj), current=saferepr(obj)
279             )
280         )
281     if isinstance(obj, functools.partial):
282         obj = obj.func
283     return obj

286 def get_real_method(obj, holder):
287     """Attempt to obtain the real function object that might be wrapping
288     ``obj``, while at the same time returning a bound method to ``holder`` if

291         is_method = hasattr(obj, "__func__")

294         return obj
295     if is_method and hasattr(obj, "__get__") and callable(obj.__get__):
296         obj = obj.__get__(holder)

375 # Perform exhaustiveness checking.
376 #
377 # Consider this example:
378 #
379 #     MyUnion = Union[int, str]
380 #
381 #     def handle(x: MyUnion) -> int {
382 #         if isinstance(x, int):
383 #             return 1
384 #         elif isinstance(x, str):
385 #             return 2
386 #         else:
387 #             raise Exception('unreachable')
388 #
389 # Now suppose we add a new variant:
390 #
391 #     MyUnion = Union[int, str, bytes]
392 #
393 # After doing this, we must remember ourselves to go and update the handle
394 # function to handle the new variant.
395 #
396 # With `assert_never` we can do better:
397 #
398 #     // raise Exception('unreachable')
399 #     return assert_never(x)
400 #
401 # Now, if we forget to handle the new variant, the type-checker will emit a
402 # compile-time error, instead of the runtime error we would have gotten
403 # previously.
404 #
405 # This also work for Enums (if you use `is` to compare) and Literals.
406 def assert_never(value: NoReturn) -> NoReturn:
407     assert False, f"Unhandled value: {value} ({type(value).__name__})"

122 def _make_xunit_fixture(
123     obj: type,
124     setup_name: str,
125     teardown_name: str,
126     cleanup_name: Optional[str],
127     scope: Scope,
128     pass_self: bool,
129 ):
130     setup = getattr(obj, setup_name, None)
131     teardown = getattr(obj, teardown_name, None)
132     if setup is None and teardown is None:
133         return None
134 
135     if cleanup_name:
136         cleanup = getattr(obj, cleanup_name, lambda *args: None)
137     else:
138 
139         def cleanup(*args):
140             pass

142     @pytest.fixture(
143         scope=scope.value,

145         # Use a unique name to speed up lookup.
146         name=f"_unittest_{setup_name}_fixture_{obj.__qualname__}",

149         if _is_skipped(self):

156                 else:
157                     setup()
158             # unittest does not call the cleanup function for every BaseException, so we
159             # follow this here.
160             except Exception:
161                 if pass_self:
162                     cleanup(self)
163                 else:
164                     cleanup()
165 
166                 raise
167         yield
168         try:
169             if teardown is not None:
170                 if pass_self:
171                     teardown(self, request.function)
172                 else:
173                     teardown()
174         finally:
175             if pass_self:
176                 cleanup(self)
177             else:
178                 cleanup()
179 
180     return fixture

375 # Perform exhaustiveness checking.

377 # Consider this example:
378 #
379 #     MyUnion = Union[int, str]
380 #
381 #     def handle(x: MyUnion) -> int {
382 #         if isinstance(x, int):
383 #             return 1

387 #             raise Exception('unreachable')

390 #
391 #     MyUnion = Union[int, str, bytes]
392 #
393 # After doing this, we must remember ourselves to go and update the handle
394 # function to handle the new variant.
395 #
396 # With `assert_never` we can do better:
397 #
398 #     // raise Exception('unreachable')
399 #     return assert_never(x)

401 # Now, if we forget to handle the new variant, the type-checker will emit a
402 # compile-time error, instead of the runtime error we would have gotten
403 # previously.
